**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity).**

**What I found**

- **Section 4.0 (Term)** locks in a three-year initial term, auto-renewing for 12-month periods subject to six months' non-renewal notice. The SOW (Section 2.0) mirrors this with a twelve-month non-renewal notice.
- **Section 5.0/5.1 (Termination)** is exclusively a *for-cause* regime: material breach with cure, insolvency events, competitor change of control, and continuing force majeure. There is no convenience right for either party.
- **Sections 5.2/5.3** are wind-down and pricing mechanics keyed to "expiration or termination for default" — they don't create an exit right, and they don't impose penalty pricing on us, so no separate redline was needed there.
- **SOW Section 6.1** lets IBM cancel Purchase Orders at any time, but that is order-level only and expressly preserves MSL's cost reimbursements — it does not give us an agreement-level exit.

**Why it fails the fallback:** the fallback contemplates customer termination on 60–90 days' notice with a capped fee. Here we have no no-cause exit at all until the end of a three-year committed term, which the playbook treats as walk-away territory.

**Direction check:** MSL is equally locked in mid-term, and its only no-cause exit (non-renewal) requires at least six months' notice — comfortably better than the 90-day floor. That side of the clause benefits us, so I left it untouched.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** a new Section 5.4 giving IBM a 30 days' notice convenience right over the Agreement, SOWs and Product Attachments, in whole or in part, with refund of prepayments, while expressly preserving MSL's entitlement to payment for Products and Parts under Sections 5.2 and 5.3 and confirming MSL gains no reciprocal mid-term convenience right.
